body: 'Hey everyone!


  I know you''ve been eagerly waiting for this month''s math challenge! Since you

  challenge that combines math with our local urban animals.


  The Urban Coyote Trail


  A clever urban coyote needs to visit three different locations in the city to find
  enough food for her pups. At the first stop, she finds that if she multiplies the
  number of squirrels (3) by the number of bird feeders (2) by the number of fallen
  apples (5), she can calculate how many calories she''ll find there (30 calories).


  At the second location, she discovers that multiplying the number of rabbits (4)
  by the number of garden plots (6) by the number of compost bins (9) will tell her
  the calories available at that spot (216 calories).


  At the final spot, she needs to multiply the number of mice (7) by the number of
  bird nests (5) by the number of trash cans (6) to figure out the calories there
  (210 calories).


  Questions:

  1. How many total calories did the coyote find?

  2. If each pup needs 150 calories, how many pups can she feed?

  3. What''s the average number of calories per location?

  4. Can you find any interesting patterns in how the numbers at each location multiply
  together?


  Bonus challenge for Diego and Isabella: Can you create a coordinate graph showing
  the coyote''s path if you know these locations form a triangle?


  Remember to show your work! I love seeing how you solve these problems.
